Asks the reader to take Ettan's place and invent a realistic intervention. That is 'go beyond the text' in the goal statement; no LO covers hypothetical perspective-taking, and C-ENG4.2-LO-3 was rejected because no story or skit is written.

Judges the relevance of the mother's line to India today -- entirely outside the text. Goal level for the same reason; the answer is an opinion with a reason, not a description (so not C-ENG4.2-LO-1).
Assertion-Reason: the student must decide whether R explains A, which is a causal judgement about the text, not a lookup. CG-ENG2 branch, unlike the plain recall MCQs in this chapter.

Assertion-Reason where R ('girls were not allowed') is false to the text -- requires testing a claim against the text. CG-ENG2 branch.
Assertion-Reason distinguishing what challenged her fear from what caused it. Causal reasoning, CG-ENG2 branch.
Assertion-Reason linking the mother's refusal to the teacher's visit. Causal reasoning, CG-ENG2 branch. (Answer carries the 'Click Here to Buy book on Amazon' advert leak.)

POEM item ('King Bruce and the Spider'), filed in this prose-titled chapter -- see report. Asks the reader to explain the poem's thesis about failure. Theme, so CG-ENG2 branch.
POEM item. Elaborates the idea that anyone can inspire -- an inference from the spider episode. CG-ENG2 branch, not retrieval.

Vocabulary exercise on endeavour/toil/strive/brace -- word meanings and use. C-ENG2.2-LO-2 (reference/vocabulary strand) rather than C-ENG3.1-LO-1, since no grammatical form is at issue. Stem is corrupted: a bare gloss ('to try very hard to achieve something') is prepended and the instruction line is missing.
POEM item: why the poet repeats 'tried and tried', 'steadily, steadily', 'up, up'. Effect of a poetic device, so the CG-ENG2 branch; C-ENG3.1-LO-1 covers grammatical categories, not repetition.

Identify metaphor vs simile in nine standalone sentences. No LO covers figures of speech: C-ENG3.1-LO-1 enumerates noun/pronoun/verb/tense/adjective/adverb only, and C-ENG2.1-LO-2 presumes a text being read. Cited at the comprehension goal, which is where understanding figurative meaning belongs.

Productive task: rewrite similes as metaphors and back. Cited at the writing goal because C-ENG4.2-LO-3 lists whole forms (stories, poems, dialogues, skits) and this is sentence-level rewriting; the recognition counterpart above got CG-ENG2.
POEM extract: why 'low' before 'despair', what image 'silken filmy clue' creates. Interpretation of diction and imagery, so CG-ENG2 branch rather than the literal-retrieval LO.
POEM extract: an analogy item, what 'Ah me!' conveys, and a reason to supply. Inferential throughout, CG-ENG2 branch.
POEM item: how the first stanza sets the mood. Craft question, CG-ENG2 branch.

POEM item: describe how King Bruce's attitude changes. Both end-states are on the page and the reader contrasts them, so retrieval in extended writing -- same treatment as the 'mother's view changed' item in batch 1.
POEM item: what the poet's detailed description reveals about his attitude. Authorial stance, never stated. CG-ENG2 branch.
POEM item: how the spider inspires us to overcome despair -- thematic application. CG-ENG2 branch. (Answer carries the 'Click Here to Buy book on Flipkart' advert leak.)

Pre-reading personal prompt, 'Who inspires you to do your best?'. Speaking about self and experience is named only in the goal, not in any LO. Stem also carries the 'NCERT TEXTUAL QUESTIONS' section banner, and the stored answer has absorbed the following pair-work picture activity.

Item from the 'Let us listen' ant-and-bird story: what the ant was known for. Answering a question on a text that happens to be heard rather than read; no LO is listening-specific, so the text-response LO is the honest fit.
